speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is happening inside you, can you tell me if you are passing gas or having bowel movements, and when your first solid foods were introduced?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The combination of an 8-month-old with feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and significant pain (crying when the belly is touched) is highly suspicious for intussusception, a common cause of bowel obstruction in this age group. I recommend an immediate Ultrasound of the abdomen to confirm the diagnosis.
